newsitem.title: USA: U.S. comptroller answers queries on DNC coffee.
newsitem.headline: U.S. comptroller answers queries on DNC coffee.

text.p: Currency Comptroller Eugene Ludwig Thursday sent hundreds of pages of documents to a House panel investigating his attendance at a White House fundraising "coffee meeting" and reiterated he did not know the nature of the event.

"I share your concern that even the appearance of political influence in the supervision of national banks should be scrupulously avoided," Ludwig said in a cover letter to House Banking Committee Chairman Jim Leach.

"That is why I have said I would not have attended the May 13 meeting if I had known representatives of the Democratic National Committee (DNC) had been invited. I reiterate that position today," he wrote.
President Clinton said last week Ludwig should have not have been invited to a May 13 meeting with Clinton, Democratic Party fund-raisers, and top banking officials.
White House officials said Ludwig's name was added to the guest list based on a misunderstanding.
The flap was the latest in the ongoing controversy about improper fundraising by the Democratic Party during the 1996 presidential campaign.
Ludwig said he, his staff and the Office of the Currency Comptroller's (OCC) chief counsel had thoroughly reviewed records and files to answer questions raised by Leach.

He said he went to only one previous DNC event, a "widely attended dinner" with Clinton and Vice President Al Gore in New York's Lincoln Centre in June 1993 and had routinely declined such invitations since then.
Three other senior staff members, who have since left the Comptroller's office, also attended DNC events, Ludwig said.

Former Senior Deputy Comptroller Konrad Alt and former senior policy adviser David Apgar attended a DNC dinner featuring the president, vice president and their wives on May 3, 1995, according to the documents.
Former Senior Deputy Comptroller Doug Harris attended the same May 3, 1995 event and another DNC dinner on May 8, 1996.

Ludwig said in the documents he contributed to the Clinton-Gore campaign in 1996. The only contact he could recall on the issue of fundraising was with a former classmate who solicited him for a contribution to the 1996 campaign.
Ludwig said he did not recall any specific conversations with OCC-regulated bankers about political contributions, adding, "and to the very best of my recollection, I never brought the subject up."
If the subject arose, Ludwig said his "practice would have been to move the discussion to another topic."

Ludwig said he first learned the May 13 meeting was set up by the DNC on Jan. 24, during press inquiries. He said he did not know the two DNC officials who attended the meeting -- former DNC Chairman Donald Fowler and former Finance Chairman Marvin Rosen -- and would not have recognised them.

The two men were included on a list of attendees faxed to him after the meeting, but they were listed as "administration participants" and Ludwig said he "would not have known of their affiliation in any event."
